config.title: Engineering metrics

intro.title: Engineering metrics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple dashboard to track and display key engineering metrics, such as deployment frequency and lead time for changes. You will learn how to define, calculate, and visualize these metrics using basic data structures and functions. The main constructs involved include variables, arrays, objects, and simple loops for data processing. This hands-on exercise will help you understand the importance of metrics in measuring team performance and guiding engineering decisions.
intro.usecase: Engineering metrics are essential for data-driven leadership in tech companies, appearing in product dashboards that track team performance, sprint velocity, and code quality. These metrics power executive reports at companies like Google and Amazon, where engineering leaders monitor deployment frequency, lead time for changes, and mean time to recovery. Practical examples include GitHub's Insights dashboard, Jira's velocity charts, and internal tools that visualize pull request throughput and incident response times. Developers implement these metrics to make informed decisions about resource allocation, process improvements, and team health assessments.

objectives: Construct a basic engineering metrics dashboard framework
Implement key performance indicator (KPI) tracking components
Configure data visualization elements for metric display
Integrate mock data sources for metric simulation
Manipulate metric thresholds and alert conditions
Initialize metric collection intervals and update mechanisms
Render metric trend analysis and historical comparisons

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library to enable component creation and state management for tracking engineering metrics.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks for a different component
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' library.

steps.title: Create the MetricsDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named MetricsDashboard that will serve as the main container for the engineering metrics application. The component should return a simple div element for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Remember to include a return statement with a div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the MetricsDashboard component below
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named MetricsDashboard is created that returns a div element, establishing the main structure for the engineering metrics dashboard.
successCriteria: The MetricsDashboard component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a functional component named MetricsDashboard that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component named MetricsDashboard that returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize metrics state with sample data
steps.instruction: Inside your MetricsDashboard component, use useState to initialize a state variable named 'metrics' with an object containing sample engineering metrics data.
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial value object that has properties like velocity, quality, and cycleTime with sample numerical values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an object
const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: 'Alex', score: 95 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a metrics state variable initialized with sample data for key engineering metrics.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an initial object containing at least velocity, quality, and cycleTime properties with sample values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with initializing state, but make sure you're creating an object with properties for velocity, quality, and cycleTime. Each should have a sample numerical value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state properly. Use useState with an object containing sample values for velocity, quality, and cycleTime metrics.

steps.title: Define a function to update metric values
steps.instruction: Inside the MetricsDashboard component, define a function called updateMetric that takes a metric name and new value as parameters,
steps.hint: The function should accept two parameters (e.g., metricName and newValue) and use setMetrics to update the state by mapping over the existing metrics array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The updateMetric function is defined inside the component, ready to be used to modify metric values.
successCriteria: The updateMetric function is defined with two parameters and uses setMetrics to update the state by mapping over the metrics array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the function, but make sure it takes two parameters and uses setMetrics to update the state by mapping over the metrics array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetric function is not defined correctly. Ensure it's inside the component, takes two parameters, and uses setMetrics to update the state.

steps.instruction: Inside the MetricsDashboard component, return a div container with a header element containing the dashboard title 'Engineering Metrics Dashboard'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that contains a header element. The header should have the text 'Engineering Metrics Dashboard'.

steps.title: Display velocity metrics section
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a <section> element that displays the velocity metric from your state. Use the metrics array to find the velocity metric and display its name and value.
steps.hint: You can access the velocity metric by filtering or finding it in the metrics array. Display it in a heading and paragraph.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a dedicated section for velocity metrics with its current value displayed.
successCriteria: A <section> element is added inside the main container, displaying the velocity metric's name and value from the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a section, but make sure it displays the velocity metric's name and value from the state array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The velocity metrics section is missing or incorrect. Ensure you're accessing the velocity metric from the state and displaying it in a <section>.

steps.title: Display quality metrics section
steps.instruction: Add a section that displays defect rate and code review coverage metrics from the state. Create a new <div> with a heading for 'Quality Metrics' and display the values from the 'Quality' and 'Satisfaction' metrics in the state.
steps.hint: You can access the metrics array from the state. Use the second and third items in the metrics array (indexes 1 and 2) which correspond to 'Quality' and 'Satisfaction' metrics.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Displaying metrics from state

Performance Metrics

Score: {metrics[0].value}

Rating: {metrics[1].value}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a 'Quality Metrics' section showing defect rate and code review coverage values from the state.
successCriteria: A new section with 'Quality Metrics' heading is added, displaying the values from the 'Quality' and 'Satisfaction' metrics in the state array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure, but make sure to display both the 'Quality' and 'Satisfaction' metric values from the state array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The quality metrics section is missing or incomplete. Add a section with a 'Quality Metrics' heading that displays the values from the 'Quality' and 'Satisfaction' metrics in the state.

steps.title: Display cycle time metrics section
steps.instruction: Add a new section inside the main container to display cycle time metrics from your state. This section should have a heading 'Cycle Time Metrics' and display the average cycle time and lead time values.
steps.hint: You can add a new <div> after the quality metrics section with a heading and paragraphs showing the relevant metric values from your state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a new metrics section

Cycle Time Metrics

Average Cycle Time: 5 days

Lead Time: 8 days
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard now includes a dedicated section for cycle time metrics with appropriate headings and values displayed.
successCriteria: A new section with heading 'Cycle Time Metrics' is added, displaying average cycle time and lead time values from the metrics state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a section, but make sure it includes the heading 'Cycle Time Metrics' and displays both average cycle time and lead time values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cycle time metrics section isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added it inside the main container with the correct structure.

steps.title: Add metric update controls and wire to handler
steps.instruction: Inside the component, add an input field with a label for each metric in the metrics state. For each input, set its value to the metric's current value and wire its onChange event to call updateMetric with the metric name and the new numeric value from the input.
steps.hint: You'll need to map over the metrics array to create a label and input for each metric. Use the metric's name as the label and for the onChange handler. Remember to convert the input string value to a number.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard will display interactive input fields for each metric (Velocity, Quality, Satisfaction) that allow users to modify the metric values. Each input will show the current metric value and update the state when changed.
successCriteria: Three labeled input fields are rendered (one for each metric). Each input's value is bound to its metric's current value. Each input's onChange event calls updateMetric with the correct metric name and numeric value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but check that all three metrics have inputs and that each onChange properly calls updateMetric with the metric name and numeric value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric update controls are missing or incomplete. Make sure to create an input for each metric with proper value binding and onChange handlers.

steps.title: Add summary visualization of metrics
steps.instruction: Add a summary section at the end of your component's return statement that displays color-coded status indicators (green/yellow/red) based on whether each metric meets target thresholds. Use inline styles or className to set background colors.
steps.hint: You can map through the metrics array and render a div for each metric. Determine the color based on the metric's value: green for good (e.g., value >= 80), yellow for warning (e.g., value >= 60), red for critical (e.g., value < 60).
steps.expectedOutcome: A summary section appears at the bottom of the dashboard with color-coded indicators (green/yellow/red) for each metric, visually representing their status against thresholds.
successCriteria: The component includes a summary section that maps through the metrics state and displays each metric with a background color determined by its value (e.g., green for high values, red for low values).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a summary section, but it may not fully implement color-coded status indicators based on thresholds. Ensure each metric displays with a background color (green/yellow/red) determined by its value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The summary visualization is missing or doesn't map through metrics to show color-coded status indicators. Review the instruction to add a section that visually represents metric status with colors.
